validity.recommendation: Change Status from 'construction' to 'operating' and revise StartYear1 from 2025 (a stale future date) to ~2017 — see status_reviews entry for full evidence and proposed_refs.
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded Status='construction' with StartYear1=2025 looks stale/wrong, not just unsourced. SNGPL's own FY2025 Annual Report (sngpl.com.pk/download/AnnualReport-2025/SNGPLAR2025.pdf), on its p.76 'Milestones' page (a historical-achievements timeline, NOT a future-plans page — confirmed by the table of contents entry '76 Milestones' and by every other entry on that page being past-tense completed work), lists 'PROJECT X (PHASE III): 16"-42" dia x 762 KM long Qadirpur–Lahore Pipeline along with installation of 25,000 HP Compression [to transport] gas downstream Sawan up to Lahore' as a completed item, immediately adjacent to 'PROJECT X (PHASE IV): 30"/24" dia x 149 KM long spurs...for supply of RLNG to Power Plants i.e. Bhikki, Balloki, Haveli Bahadur Shah and Nandipur' (also completed). This matches GEM's P3178 almost exactly on route (Sawan/Qadirpur→Lahore), diameter ceiling (42in), and stated purpose (RLNG transport downstream of Sawan) — GEM's 770km sits inside the 750–780km band every source uses for this same corridor (see the confirmed-caveat entry below). Independently, nsenergybusiness.com's Bhikki power-plant page states the plant's RLNG 'is supplied...through an 18km spur gas pipeline connected with SNGPL's Qilla Sattar Shah to Bhikki pipeline' — Qilla Sattar Shah near Lahore is the exact terminus named in the original 2017 sanction press (offshore-energy.biz: '42-inch pipeline from Sawan to Qilla Satar Shah, near Lahore (780km)'), confirming that trunk is built and live. Further independently, Dawn (dawn.com/news/1368494, Nov 2017) reports LNG-terminal maintenance forcing supply curtailments to Bhikki, Haveli Bahadur Shah, Balloki and Nandipur ('85MMCFD is being supplied to Balloki, Nandipur-31MMCFD' etc.) — i.e. these plants were already drawing RLNG through this network by November 2017, years before GEM's recorded 2025 start. Three independent, non-GEM sources (SNGPL's own corporate report, an industry trade outlet, and a national newspaper) converge on the same conclusion: the trunk is built and has been moving RLNG since 2017–18, not 'under construction' toward a still-future 2025 start. Filed as a spec/status concern rather than existence — the pipeline unquestionably exists; what's wrong is the lifecycle stage recorded for it. Full sourcing/verdict in the status_reviews array below (do not also treat this as a fill for Status[ref] or Start[ref] — those are marked UNRESOLVED, not confirmed, since I am NOT supporting the current values).

validity.recommendation: Re-derive SegmentCost — the currently recorded $672,000,000 USD does not reconcile with the sourced PKR figure at a contemporaneous exchange rate; flag for correction rather than pasting a ref that would falsely appear to confirm it.
validity.researcher_notes: The original sanction press (offshore-energy.biz, 6 Mar 2017, verified OK; also reported by Express Tribune 2017, verified via Wayback) states the total investment as 'PKR 110.5 billion (approximately US$1 billion)' for this exact project (1,200mmcfd capacity, Sawan–Qilla Satar Shah stage). PKR110.51bn at the 2017 exchange rate (~PKR104–105/USD) is ~US$1.05–1.06 billion — consistent with the source's own 'approximately US$1 billion' gloss. GEM's recorded SegmentCost of $672,000,000 implies an effective rate of ~PKR164/USD, which is a mid-2022/2023-era rate, not a 2017 one. This looks like a currency-conversion-year mismatch (the PKR figure converted at a much-later, post-devaluation rate rather than the rate contemporaneous with the 2017 sanction), the same class of defect already logged elsewhere in this project as a length-units/exchange-rate hazard. I could not find an independent, more recent PKR figure that would justify $672M as a genuinely lower re-estimated cost (no cost-overrun-reduction or re-scoping story turned up), so I'm not proposing a replacement number — just flagging the number as unreconciled and worth a human re-check of the original entry's conversion math. Leaving SegmentCost [ref] UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating support for a value I believe is arithmetically off.

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and well-documented, not a GEM-only entity. Independently confirmed by Express Tribune 2017 ('SNGPL gives green light to Karachi-Lahore LNG pipeline', via Wayback), The News 2017 (Sindh ROW grant for the Karachi-Sawan companion segment, via Wayback), offshore-energy.biz (Mar 2017 sanction), World Pipelines/GlobalData (Jan 2022, 770km exact match to GEM), offshore-technology.com/GlobalData (762km, max dia 42in), and SNGPL's own FY2025 annual report. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType='transmission' and Fuel='Gas' both correct — this is unambiguously a large-diameter (16–42in), multi-hundred-km trunk moving RLNG/gas from the Sawan/Qadirpur interconnection to the Lahore-area distribution grid, not a gathering or feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the 6-pipeline in-scope roster (P0452 Iran-Pakistan, P0766 TAPI, P3101 Pakistan Stream, P3173 Somiani-Nawabshah, P3174 Off-Shore, P3178 itself) — no overlap; all are geographically and functionally distinct. Note for context (not a roster duplicate): the companion Karachi-to-Sawan segment is built by SSGC and tracked by GEM as a SEPARATE pipeline ('Karachi–Sawan Gas Pipeline'), which is the correct way to segment this by owner/operator at the Sawan interconnection — not a double-count with P3178. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL)' at 100% is confirmed by every source — SNGPL's board sanctioned, financed, and built this segment. LENGTH: GEM's 770km sits within the range every independent source uses for this same corridor (750km per one search summary, 762km per SNGPL's own Phase-III figure and GlobalData/offshore-technology, 770km per World Pipelines/GlobalData, 780km per the original 2017 Sawan-to-Qilla-Satar-Shah figure) — the spread reflects different endpoint conventions (Sawan vs. Qadirpur as the nominal start) rather than a wrong value, so treated as confirmed with a caveat rather than a spec concern. CAPACITY: 1200 MMcf/d matches the original 2017 board-approved figure exactly (offshore-energy.biz, corroborated by the Tribune/PSX-filing figure). DIAMETER: GEM's Diameter field was blank; see fills — filled as a range (16–42in) rather than one number because the pipe genuinely tapers across sub-segments, not because of missing precision.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Recorded Status='construction' with StartYear1=2025 (i.e. a still-future start) does not survive a check against SNGPL's own current corporate reporting. SNGPL's FY2025 Annual Report puts the near-identical project (16"-42" dia x 762km 'Qadirpur-Lahore Pipeline' + 25,000HP compression, 'gas downstream Sawan up to Lahore') on its p.76 'Milestones' page — a page of completed historical achievements (confirmed by TOC entry '76 Milestones' and by every neighboring entry being past-tense: Phase II 'was undertaken to transport additional 400 MMCFD RLNG downstream Sawan', Phase IV 'was laid for supply of RLNG to Power Plants i.e. Bhikki, Balloki, Haveli Bahadur Shah and Nandipur'). That Phase IV entry names the exact four RLNG power plants this trunk feeds. Independently, nsenergybusiness.com's Bhikki project page confirms the plant draws RLNG via an 18km spur off 'SNGPL's Qilla Sattar Shah to Bhikki pipeline' — Qilla Sattar Shah being the precise near-Lahore terminus named in the original 2017 sanction reporting for THIS pipeline (offshore-energy.biz: '42-inch pipeline from Sawan to Qilla Satar Shah, near Lahore, 780km'). And Dawn (Nov 2017) reports LNG-terminal-maintenance supply curtailments actually being applied to Bhikki/Balloki/Haveli Bahadur Shah/Nandipur with specific MMCFD figures — i.e. gas was demonstrably flowing to these plants via this network by November 2017. Three independent sources (SNGPL itself, an industry trade outlet, a national newspaper), none tracing to GEM or to each other, converge on: this trunk was built and moving RLNG by 2017, not merely 'under construction' toward a 2025 start that has by now already passed without incident in any source I found. I'm proposing StartYear1=2017 as the best-evidenced anchor (Dawn's Nov-2017 evidence of active flow) rather than a precise commissioning month, which I could not pin down further; a human should ideally cross-check against SNGPL's earlier (e.g. FY2017-18) annual report for an exact commissioning date/month before finalizing. Tier=high on the strength of three independent, differently-sourced confirmations; residual uncertainty is only about the EXACT month of the status change, not the direction of it. Did not attempt a staleness-rule demotion (the dormancy rules in the SOP apply to proposed/shelved decay, not to this situation, which is a positive-evidence upgrade, not a decay inference).

summary: P3178 (Sawan-Lahore Gas Pipeline) is confirmed real, correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk, correctly attributed to SNGPL, and not a roster duplicate; but Status='construction'/StartYear1=2025 looks stale (SNGPL's own 2025 annual report + independent Bhikki-plant/Dawn 2017 reporting indicate this trunk was actually built and moving RLNG by 2017 -> proposed status_reviews change to Status=operating/StartYear1=2017), and SegmentCost=$672M does not reconcile with the sourced PKR110.51bn figure at a contemporaneous exchange rate (flagged, not fixed). 7 refs added (Fuel, PipelineType, Proposal, Capacity, Length, Location, Owner) plus a best-effort Diameter fill; Status[ref], Start[ref], and SegmentCost[ref] left UNRESOLVED on purpose rather than falsely confirming values I believe are wrong.
